# Project Summary - User Registration System
## ✅ What's Currently Implemented
### 1. **Project Structure** - ✅ Maven-based Spring Boot 3.5.8 project with Java 17 - ✅ Clean package structure: `controller`, `model`, `dto` - ✅ Follows standard Spring Boot conventions
### 2. **Core Classes**
#### Main.java - Spring Boot application entry point - Uses `@SpringBootApplication` annotation
#### User.java (Model) ``` Fields: id, firstName, lastName, age, city Full getters/setters + toString() ```
#### UserController.java ``` Endpoints: - GET / → Welcome message - GET /get-all-users → Returns all users (ArrayList) - POST /add-user → Adds new user with ApiResponse wrapper ```
#### ApiResponse.java (DTO) ``` Generic response wrapper with: - status (String) - message (String) - data (T - generic) - timestamp (LocalDateTime - auto-generated) ```
### 3. **Current Capabilities** - ✅ RESTful API endpoints working - ✅ JSON request/response handling - ✅ Generic response wrapper for consistency - ✅ In-memory data storage (ArrayList) - ✅ HTTP status codes (200 OK, 201 CREATED)
## What's Missing (Next Steps)
### Priority 1 - Database Integration - [ ] Add Spring Data JPA dependency - [ ] Add MySQL/PostgreSQL driver - [ ] Create UserRepository interface - [ ] Create application.properties with DB config - [ ] Add @Entity annotation to User model - [ ] Change id to Long with @Id @GeneratedValue
### Priority 2 - Service Layer - [ ] Create UserService interface - [ ] Create UserServiceImpl with business logic - [ ] Move ArrayList logic from controller to service - [ ] Add proper error handling
### Priority 3 - Validation & Error Handling - [ ] Add Spring Validation dependency - [ ] Add @Valid annotations and constraints - [ ] Create GlobalExceptionHandler with @ControllerAdvice - [ ] Handle ResourceNotFoundException, ValidationException, etc.
### Priority 4 - Additional CRUD Operations - [ ] GET /users/{id} - Get user by ID - [ ] PUT /users/{id} - Update user - [ ] DELETE /users/{id} - Delete user - [ ] Add pagination/sorting to GET all users
### Priority 5 - Security (Authentication) - [ ] Add Spring Security dependency - [ ] Add password field to User model - [ ] Implement BCrypt password encoding - [ ] Add email field for login - [ ] Implement JWT authentication - [ ] Secure endpoints with @PreAuthorize
## Current Architecture
``` Request → Controller → ArrayList → Response (Direct) (In-Memory) ```
## Target Architecture
``` Request → Controller → Service → Repository → Database (Business (JPA/Hibernate) (MySQL/PostgreSQL) Logic) ```
## Dependencies to Add
```xml <!-- Database --> <dependency> <groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId> <artifactId>spring-boot-starter-data-jpa</artifactId> </dependency>
<dependency> <groupId>com.mysql</groupId> <artifactId>mysql-connector-j</artifactId> <scope>runtime</scope> </dependency>
<!-- Validation --> <dependency> <groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId> <artifactId>spring-boot-starter-validation</artifactId> </dependency>
<!-- Lombok (Optional but recommended) --> <dependency> <groupId>org.projectlombok</groupId> <artifactId>lombok</artifactId> <optional>true</optional> </dependency>
<!-- Security --> <dependency> <groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId> <artifactId>spring-boot-starter-security</artifactId> </dependency>
<!-- JWT --> <dependency> <groupId>io.jsonwebtoken</groupId> <artifactId>jjwt-api</artifactId> <version>0.11.5</version> </dependency> ```
## Quick Reference
### Current API Testing
**Start Application:** ```bash mvn spring-boot:run ```
**Test Welcome:** ```bash curl http://localhost:8080/ ```
**Add User:** ```bash curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/add-user ^ -H "Content-Type: application/json" ^ -d "{\"id\":1,\"firstName\":\"John\",\"lastName\":\"Doe\",\"age\":30,\"city\":\"New York\"}" ```
**Get All Users:** ```bash curl http://localhost:8080/get-all-users ```
### PowerShell Alternative: ```powershell $user = @{id=1; firstName="John"; lastName="Doe"; age=30; city="NYC"} | ConvertTo-Json Invoke-RestMethod -Uri "http://localhost:8080/add-user" -Method Post -Body $user -ContentType "application/json" ```
## Development Roadmap
1. **Week 1-2**: Database Integration + Service Layer 2. **Week 3**: Validation + Error Handling + Complete CRUD 3. **Week 4**: Authentication (Spring Security + JWT) 4. **Week 5**: Testing (Unit + Integration) 5. **Week 6**: Advanced Features (Email verification, password reset) 6. **Week 7+**: Deployment + Documentation (Swagger)
## Learning Resources
- [Spring Boot Documentation](https://docs.spring.io/spring-boot/docs/current/reference/htmlsingle/) - [Spring Data JPA](https://docs.spring.io/spring-data/jpa/docs/current/reference/html/) - [Spring Security](https://docs.spring.io/spring-security/reference/) - [RESTful API Best Practices](https://restfulapi.net/)
--- **Last Updated**: December 17, 2025

# Quick Start Guide
This guide will help you get the User Registration System up and running in 5 minutes.
## Prerequisites Check
Before starting, verify you have: - ✅ Java 17+ installed (`java -version`) - ✅ Maven 3.6+ installed (`mvn -version`) - ✅ Your favorite IDE ready (IntelliJ IDEA, Eclipse, VS Code)
## Step 1: Get the Code
```bash git clone https://github.com/PasinduOG/Project-01-Spring-Boot.git cd Project-01-Spring-Boot ```
## Step 2: Build the Project
```bash mvn clean install ```
This will: - Download all dependencies - Compile the code - Run tests (if any) - Create a JAR file in `target/`
## ▶️ Step 3: Run the Application
Choose one of these methods:
### Method A: Using Maven ```bash mvn spring-boot:run ```
### Method B: Using Java ```bash java -jar target/Project-01-Spring-Boot-1.0-SNAPSHOT.jar ```
### Method C: Using IDE - Open the project in your IDE - Navigate to `src/main/java/com/example/Main.java` - Right-click and select "Run Main.main()"
You should see: ``` Started Main in X.XXX seconds ```
## Step 4: Test the API
### Test 1: Welcome Message ```bash curl http://localhost:8080/ ``` **Expected:** `Welcome to User Management System`
### Test 2: Add a User
**Using cURL:** ```bash curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/add-user \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"id":1,"firstName":"John","lastName":"Doe","age":30,"city":"New York"}' ```
**Using PowerShell:** ```powershell $user = @{ id = 1 firstName = "John" lastName = "Doe" age = 30 city = "New York" } | ConvertTo-Json
Invoke-RestMethod -Uri "http://localhost:8080/add-user" -Method Post -Body $user -ContentType "application/json" ```
**Expected Response:** ```json { "status": "success", "message": "User registered successfully", "data": { "id": 1, "firstName": "John", "lastName": "Doe", "age": 30, "city": "New York" }, "timestamp": "2025-12-17T10:30:45.123" } ```
### Test 3: Get All Users ```bash curl http://localhost:8080/get-all-users ```
**Expected Response:** ```json [ { "id": 1, "firstName": "John", "lastName": "Doe", "age": 30, "city": "New York" } ] ```
## Using Postman (Recommended)
1. **Install Postman** (if not already installed) - Download from: https://www.postman.com/downloads/
2. **Import Collection** (Optional) - Create a new collection called "User Registration System" - Add requests for each endpoint
3. **Test Endpoints:**
**GET /** - URL: `http://localhost:8080/` - Method: GET
**POST /add-user** - URL: `http://localhost:8080/add-user` - Method: POST - Headers: `Content-Type: application/json` - Body (raw JSON): ```json { "id": 1, "firstName": "Jane", "lastName": "Smith", "age": 28, "city": "San Francisco" } ```
**GET /get-all-users** - URL: `http://localhost:8080/get-all-users` - Method: GET
## Troubleshooting
### Problem: "Port 8080 already in use" **Solution:** - Find and kill the process using port 8080, OR - Change the port by adding to `src/main/resources/application.properties`: ```properties server.port=8081 ```
### Problem: "mvn: command not found" **Solution:** - Verify Maven is installed: https://maven.apache.org/install.html - Add Maven to your PATH environment variable
### Problem: "Java version mismatch" **Solution:** - Verify Java 17+ is installed and set as default - Check with: `java -version`
### Problem: "Cannot connect to localhost:8080" **Solution:** - Ensure the application started successfully (check console for errors) - Verify no firewall is blocking port 8080 - Try: `http://127.0.0.1:8080/` instead
## What's Next?
Now that you have the basic system running, you can:
1. **Explore the Code:** - Check out `UserController.java` to see how endpoints work - Look at `ApiResponse.java` to understand the response wrapper - Review `User.java` to see the data model
2. **Add More Users:** - Try adding multiple users with different IDs - View all users using `/get-all-users`
3. **Learn & Extend:** - Read `PROJECT_SUMMARY.md` for development roadmap - Check `README.md` for detailed documentation - Start with "Priority 1" tasks (Database Integration)
## Recommended Learning Path
If you're new to Spring Boot:
1. **Basics** (Current) - ✅ Understand REST API concepts - ✅ Learn Spring Boot project structure - ✅ Practice testing with Postman/cURL
2. **Database** (Week 1-2) - Learn Spring Data JPA - Set up MySQL/PostgreSQL - Create repositories and entities
3. **Validation** (Week 3) - Add Bean Validation - Implement error handling - Complete CRUD operations
4. **Security** (Week 4) - Add Spring Security - Implement JWT authentication - Secure endpoints
## Pro Tips
- **Keep the app running** while testing - it's fast to restart if needed - **Use Postman Collections** to save your test requests - **Check the console** for detailed logs and error messages - **Read the README** for comprehensive documentation - **Start small** - master the basics before adding complex features
## Need Help?
- Check the full **README.md** for detailed information - Review **PROJECT_SUMMARY.md** for architecture overview - Search Spring Boot documentation: https://spring.io/projects/spring-boot - Look for similar examples on GitHub
---
**Happy Coding! **
If you got this far, you're ready to start developing. Begin by adding database integration or create your own endpoints!
